notes.title: JUNE 3RD BLOG UPDATE
notes.notes:
Another week, another post, here’s what we’ve been doing lately :)
---

[h1]UI[/h1]
If you’ve opted into the experimental builds, you probably know that all the UI has now been ported over to Unity’s native UI system. It’s all functional, but not complete. A lot of animations and effects are missing.

I had a fun issue the day of uploading our latest experimental build. I had finished porting over all the UI and went to test it in the standalone build. The menus were not appearing or they were at random locations on the screen. I managed to fumble around and start a new game, and then quit back to the main menu. The menus were now appearing correctly. Huh?

Unity’s UI system has an option to render a UI “canvas” as a screen overlay, through a camera or in the game’s world space. We’re rendering our UI elements as a screen overlay so we don’t need additional cameras or culling layers for them. In the main menu scene, there’s no need for a camera at the moment - it’s just the menus. What’s not immediately apparent is that if you don’t have ANY camera in the scene, overlay canvases will not render correctly. A Unity tech explained that without a camera, the screen overlay canvas has nothing to “overlay”. Uhh.. makes sense :P So chucking in a dummy camera rendering nothing was enough to trigger a clear and tell the canvases to overlay that and do their thing. It was an odd one, and I’ll put it down to a long day, but the 0.04.E2 build ended up being released a day later because of it. It happens.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
A lot of materials were broken with the move to Unity 5 for the experimental branch. Don’t be surprised if you see objects with incorrect specular, missing normal maps or odd colors. Anything that’s meant to be glass or transparent will also display as a solid color as we haven’t gotten around to writing a glass shader compatible with the new lighting model. Handling materials in Unity 5 is also a bit buggy, which hasn’t been helping. Bug reports and repro projects have been submitted, but no news so far.

[h1]Speedtree[/h1]
As mentioned in recent posts, we’ve incorporated Speedtree into our workflow with the move to Unity 5. It comes with its pros and cons.

It’s fantastic for our early access workflow to have full control of wind parameters, LOD’s, billboards, ambient occlusion, and texture atlasing inside the one program. Before Speedtree, this process took much longer and relied on a number of different programs, which in some cases had worse results and made it nearly impossible to make fast edits without repeating the whole process again.

Speedtree is great software but it could definitely use some improvements with its Unity integration, such as the lack of physically-based shader support and nit-picky duplicated material exports. We’ve also had issues with getting funky results for vertex normal directions for leaf meshes which we’re looking into.

[h1]Coop[/h1]
We’re starting to look into coop. Co-op isn’t a high priority on our list as a feature - we’ve always said that we’re focusing on a solid single player game first - but we’re going to be rewriting a lot of existing systems, so now’s the time to get the basics implemented as a lot of the new systems will need to build on it. Basically, if we don’t lay the foundation for co-op now, we’ll end up needing to rewrite a lot of code to support it, or even worse, tack on or duplicate existing functionality for coop gameplay.

There are some problems and choices to be made. If you’ve played the game, you’ve probably noticed that Stranded Deep relies on a lot of physics, picking things up, throwing them around, etc. In general, physics and networking is a pain. We’re still looking into it, but there might be some compromises and changes. Right now we’re running tests and looking into the best way to synchronise everything.

[h1]Terrain[/h1]
The world in Stranded Deep is currently procedurally generated and infinite. This has worked great for development; features have been easy to add and everybody has gotten around to testing them. Soon though, we’ll be creating a large hand-crafted tile-based world. This will allow us to slowly “create” the world as we progress, adding a new tile with a new island or landmark as that part of the world is designed. There will be small tropical atolls dotted around the world (similar to now) and larger, more interesting islands as landmarks, where you might prefer to setup camp.

We also have plans to implement world building tools for the community. So potentially, you would design your tile’s terrain externally in World Machine, etc and then import your terrain data and create your own island tile with our provided tools. Other users would then be able to download your island and assign it to a free tile in their game. It’s in conceptual stages at the moment, but that’s essentially the idea.

 
Larger islands and coop are two of our most requested features, so we’re pretty excited to be working on both of them :) Between the new terrain system and coop, this is where most of our time is going. So hopefully you can understand that the next experimental build might not be released until we have something that’s playable. But we’ll always keep you updated on our progress on our blog :)

 
Stay Alive!
:: Beam Team

notes.title: LATEST UPDATE: 0.03.H2
notes.notes:
Hi guys, 

Hotfix 2 for version 0.03 (0.03.H2) is now live. 

[h1][i]There’s been some changes to the way the save system works so please read the important notes on backing up your existing save file and setting it up for this build at the end of this post..[/i][/h1]

Now, this month’s update is a small one. It’s probably the least content we’ve released in an update so far …and there’s a reason for it. 
We had to make a big call for this update. We were working on some big systems this month and last week we realised we weren’t going to get them done for this update. So we’ve had to pull a lot of content from this update. This highlighted a bigger problem that’s become more and more evident as the game’s development has progressed under Early Access - working to a monthly build has been very prohibiting. Our monthly builds need to be stable enough so that you’re not losing you’re progress every update. It’s just not fun playing a game in pieces. But at the same time we need to move forward and the things we want to move forward with are going to break the game ...a lot. What to do? Well starting as of this update, version 0.03 will remain the stable build and in the next few weeks we’ll be starting a new experimental branch that players can opt into. The experimental build will be just that, highly experimental. It will allow us a lot more freedom in development and will allow you to see more immediate progress of the things we’re working on. Because you won’t be seeing that progress reflected in the stable build which most players will be playing, we’ll be going back to fortnightly blog updates on our website how we used to, to keep you up to date with what we’re working on. And of course we’ll be uploading the experimental builds if you want to check it out.

We have a lot of big things planned. Some of them include:
[list][*]Moving over to Unity 5.
[*]Reworking the terrain system.
[*]Reworking the ocean - Better and bigger wave animations and more complete buoyancy.
[*]Reworking a lot of behind the scenes for co-operative game play.
[*]Incorporating a proper player model with shadows and animations.
[*]Creating an actual audio system.
[*]A new loot system incorporating proper scavenging mechanics.
[*]Improving the construction system to build on the new scavenging system to create more unique structures.
[*]A tool crafting system – scavenging different handles, bindings and blades to create unique tools and weapons. 
Improving the weather with procedural cloud cover and better weather events.
[*]A map editor and modding tools.
[*]Heaps more…[/list]
We’ll be posting a blog post in the next few days with more details and concept art on what we have planned for the above so stay posted. 

The main point of all this is that we don’t want Stranded Deep to turn into an early access game where you come back in a few months and updates time and it basically looks like the exact same game - a game where “progress” is made every month, but nothing really changes or grows into something better. It’s been a hard call to make this month, but we know it’s the right one. We have big plans and are pretty excited so we hope you’ll understand and support us as we do that :)

We’ll post an announcement soon with more details on the experimental build.

Stay Alive!
:: Beam Team 
---


[h1]0.03.H2 CHANGE LOG[/h1]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[b]Raft Motor[/b] – Now requires a hammer to be built.
[b]Fire Spit[/b] – Now updates display name when attached cookable is cooked.
[b]Shipwrecks[/b] – Fixed visual error with glass shader not blending with fog.
[b]Crafting[/b] – Fixed “lashing” material name incorrectly appearing as “rope” in crafting option’s material list.
[b]Building[/b] – Fixed a bug where foundations would default to a raft when snapping to an existing foundation over water.
[b]HUD Information Option[/b] – Fixed a bug where toggling the display of item names was not applying in game.
[b]Input Options[/b] – Fixed a rather annoying bug for players where mouse buttons were reassigning as the mouse axis.
[b]Goggles, Flippers and Torch[/b] – Added a notification for now to notify player that these items have been equipped.
[b]Flying[/b] – The last known dragging-flying exploit, aka the “broomstick” method, has been fixed.
[b]Water Bottles[/b] – Fixed a bug with all food items not saving data. This would result in water bottles refilling when loaded back, etc.
[b]Rafts[/b] – Adjusted ladder colliders for wooden rafts for easier climbing.
[b]Crabs[/b] – Fixed immortal crabs when cooking alive. Crabs now die if you cook them alive by dragging onto a fire, etc. 
[b]Rain[/b] – Fixed weather effects not having appropriate filter when underwater.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[b]Saving[/b] – It’s now possible to have multiple save game files. Your save file is now saved local to the game’s installation in a folder named after your Steam ID. It may look like a random series of numbers but it actually corresponds to your unique user ID on Steam. It’s worth mentioning that there are a few ways to identify your Steam ID if you need to. A quick google search will help here. 
[b]Saving[/b] – Internal optimisations to save file parser.
[b]World Seed[/b] – You can now share your world seed. You will be prompted to input a world seed when you select “New Game” on the main menu. You can view your world seed on the bottom right corner of the pause menu.
[b]Player[/b] – More randomized and more variety of player sound effects. Improved jumping sounds and more variety. Improved landing sounds and more variety. Vomitting sounds effects. Improved breathing sounds effects
[b]Label Maker[/b] – New item! A small side item that introduces a new mechanic to rename items if that’s your thing.

[h1]Balancing[/h1]
[b]Sharks[/b] – Dynamically adjusted circling radius based on the damage dealt to the shark.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Less crazy raft bumping!
[b]Sharks[/b] – Temporary fix to spamming damage by holding down the use item key.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Will lose interest in players when on land.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Increased maximum damage: Tiger Sharks from 1000 to 2250, Great whites from 2000 to 3350.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Regain 0.5 health per second after 320 seconds have passed since last receiving damage.
[b]Balance[/b] - Adjusted compass model holding view.
[b]Balance[/b] – Decreased various fish spawn chances. Sharks are now much rarer.
[list][*]Tiger shark from 100% to 30%, 
[*]Great White from 100% to 18%, 
[*]Reef Sharks from 100% to 25%, 
[*]Marlin from 100% to 25%, 
[*]Whales from 20% to 6%, 
[*]Stingrays from 100% to 65%,
[*]Turtles from 100% to 55%.[/list]
[b]Balance[/b] – Loot container item spawn chance. Container slots now have a slight chance for spawning nothing (average 90% to spawn).

[h1]Restoring your save file Instructions[/h1]
Backup your save file by locating you Steam Apps folder (Google to the rescue here again) and inside the Stranded Deep folder you will find a folder called “Data” and inside that you will find your save file under “Save.json”.
The easiest way to transfer the contents is to start the game to the main menu and then quit the game. A new folder will have been created in the Stranded Deep folder corresponding to your Steam ID. (It may look like a random series of numbers but it actually corresponds to your unique user ID on Steam). Copy your existing “Save.json” save file into the new folder. Rename the save file with the same name as the folder it’s now in. 
Done :)

[b]Fire Spit[/b] – Now updates display name when attached cookable is cooked.
[b]Shipwrecks[/b] – Fixed visual error with glass shader not blending with fog.
[b]Crafting[/b] – Fixed “lashing” material name incorrectly appearing as “rope” in crafting option’s material list.
[b]Building[/b] – Fixed a bug where foundations would default to a raft when snapping to an existing foundation over water.
[b]HUD Information Option[/b] – Fixed a bug where toggling the display of item names was not applying in game.
[b]Input Options[/b] – Fixed a rather annoying bug for players where mouse buttons were reassigning as the mouse axis.
[b]Goggles, Flippers and Torch[/b] – Added a notification for now to notify player that these items have been equipped.
[b]Flying[/b] – The last known dragging-flying exploit, aka the “broomstick” method, has been fixed.
[b]Water Bottles[/b] – Fixed a bug with all food items not saving data. This would result in water bottles refilling when loaded back, etc.
[b]Rafts[/b] – Adjusted ladder colliders for wooden rafts for easier climbing.
[b]Crabs[/b] – Fixed immortal crabs when cooking alive. Crabs now die if you cook them alive by dragging onto a fire, etc. 
[b]Rain[/b] – Fixed weather effects not having appropriate filter when underwater.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[b]Saving[/b] – It’s now possible to have multiple save game files. Your save file is now saved local to the game’s installation in a folder named after your Steam ID. It may look like a random series of numbers but it actually corresponds to your unique user ID on Steam. It’s worth mentioning that there are a few ways to identify your Steam ID if you need to. A quick google search will help here. 
[b]Saving[/b] – Internal optimisations to save file parser.
[b]World Seed[/b] – You can now share your world seed. You will be prompted to input a world seed when you select “New Game” on the main menu. You can view your world seed on the bottom right corner of the pause menu.
[b]Player[/b] – More randomized and more variety of player sound effects. Improved jumping sounds and more variety. Improved landing sounds and more variety. Vomitting sounds effects. Improved breathing sounds effects
[b]Label Maker[/b] – New item! A small side item that introduces a new mechanic to rename items if that’s your thing.

[h1]Balancing[/h1]
[b]Sharks[/b] – Dynamically adjusted circling radius based on the damage dealt to the shark.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Less crazy raft bumping!
[b]Sharks[/b] – Temporary fix to spamming damage by holding down the use item key.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Will lose interest in players when on land.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Increased maximum damage: Tiger Sharks from 1000 to 2250, Great whites from 2000 to 3350.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Regain 0.5 health per second after 320 seconds have passed since last receiving damage.
[b]Balance[/b] - Adjusted compass model holding view.
[b]Balance[/b] – Decreased various fish spawn chances. Sharks are now much rarer.
[list][*]Tiger shark from 100% to 30%, 
[*]Great White from 100% to 18%, 
[*]Reef Sharks from 100% to 25%, 
[*]Marlin from 100% to 25%, 
[*]Whales from 20% to 6%, 
[*]Stingrays from 100% to 65%,
[*]Turtles from 100% to 55%.[/list]
[b]Balance[/b] – Loot container item spawn chance. Container slots now have a slight chance for spawning nothing (average 90% to spawn).

[h1]Restoring your save file Instructions[/h1]
Backup your save file by locating you Steam Apps folder (Google to the rescue here again) and inside the Stranded Deep folder you will find a folder called “Data” and inside that you will find your save file under “Save.json”.
The easiest way to transfer the contents is to start the game to the main menu and then quit the game. A new folder will have been created in the Stranded Deep folder corresponding to your Steam ID. (It may look like a random series of numbers but it actually corresponds to your unique user ID on Steam). Copy your existing “Save.json” save file into the new folder. Rename the save file with the same name as the folder it’s now in. 
Done :)

notes.title: LATEST UPDATE: 0.03
notes.notes:
Hi guys, 

Version 0.03 is now live.

The March update is here with Sea Forts, multistory building, some UI gameplay changes and plenty of bug fixes. Performance is also generally improved. This update shouldn't require a restart, but as always if you’re experiencing any problems or funny behavior, please try starting a new game before posting a bug report.

Enjoy the update :)

For more details, see the steam community hub here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/313120/discussions/0/611698195158286688/


Stay Alive!
:: Beam Team 
---


[h1][b]0.03 CHANGE LOG[/b][/h1]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[b]Cloth[/b] – Fixed spelling mistake in description.
[b]Cloth[/b] – Fixed bug with crafting trigger not activating.
[b]Paddle[/b] – Fixed a bug with paddle buoyancy flying to the surface.
[b]Foundations[/b] – Hard to replicate but hopefully fixed Items falling through foundations. Time and player feedback will tell with this one. Only other thing is possibly destroying order of things?
[b]Context Menus[/b] – Fixed context menu spam and using items when closing menus spam.
[b]Context Menus[/b] – Fixed a bug with the context menu interacting collider.
[b]Context Menus[/b] – Fixed a bug where constructing combos options were getting cut off with a long list.
[b]Crafting[/b] – Some improvement made to lag when equipping a hammer to switch between building and crafting modes with large collections and buildings. There’s a lot more work to be done here, but it should be better.
[b]Building[/b] – Improved foundation collisions. You can now walk underneath foundations and place on rocky terrain. This does allow the ability to do silly things like placing structures inside rocks, so beware.
[b]Doors[/b] – Fixed shipwreck door collisions. 
[b]Doors[/b] – Fixed all door colliders moving player when opening.
[b]Medical Supplies[/b] – Fixed bug with infinite medical supplies. 
[b]Airtank[/b] – Players seem to be a bit confused with this one so we reworked the functionality to make it less confusing and more consistent. Previously, the airtank had a set capacity and would refill your air deficit. Now it just has a set number of uses so make sure you get the best out of them.
[b]Fire Spit[/b] – Now displays the attached cookable’s name.
[b]Ocean[/b] – Fixed a bug where the ocean would turn red during weather events.
[b]Trees[/b] – Fixed a bug where cut down connected tree trunks where loading back as logs not trunks.
[b]Doors[/b] – Door model now indicates which way the door opens when placing.
[b]Steps[/b] – Building materials have been adjusted. Previously the steps were a ‘luxury’ item. Now they are a requirement for accessing second stories, so the material requirement has also been adjusted. Steps are now 4x stick, 2x Rope.
[b]Beds[/b] – Reduced size to fit inside a single foundation.
[b]Bubbles[/b] – Fixed bug where bubble markers were disappearing.
[b]Shipwrecks[/b] – Plane shipwreck now has bubble markers.
[b]Boat Motor[/b] – Fixed fuel gauge only updating when boat motor was running.
[b]Player[/b] – Changed crouching mechanic. You now have to hold the crouch key to remain crouched.
[b]Bucket[/b] – Fixed the “portal/stargate” bug.
[b]Coconuts[/b] – Fixed a rare occurrence of a missing reference.
[b]Whale[/b] – Fixed constant whale noise spam.
[b]Crabs[/b] – Fixed a bug where crabs weren’t being parented to the right node for re-centering and saving.
[b]Boat Motor[/b] – Reduced the lawn mower’s volume from 0.7 to 0.4.
[b]Effects[/b] – Fixed a bug with incorrect god rays appearing underwater (big orange blob).

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[b]Sea Forts![/b] – You can now explore a series of connected sea forts that provide great shelter and can contain various loot and supplies. Sea Forts are procedurally generated in the sand plains biome. Please note that we are working on a much more improved billboard system for the future so sea fort transitions may be jerky/sudden when loading biomes at this stage in development.
[b]Multistory Building![/b] – Official multistory building. This system is a work in progress and is in alpha stage and will be constantly evolving. There are currently a very few edge cases with unrealistic placements that will get cleaned up as the system progresses and finalizes. There’s no limitations on stories for now, so we can’t wait for the mega tower screenshots! We’ll be incorporating things like structural material limitations and more advanced destruction in future updates.
[b]Interacting[/b] – New mechanic for interacting with objects! To interact with interactive objects like campfires, consoles and containers, hold the left mouse button down momentarily when the new interacting icon appears. Similarly, the crafting context menu icon has a new look.
Clicking with the left mouse button will use your current item on the object you’re looking at, as normal.
This mechanic opens up the ability to be able to destroy interactive items like campfires and doors, which has not been possible until now.
[b]Steps[/b] – Steps functionality has been changed. When placing, you can rotate the orientation of the stairs to point in the direction you want. However, stairs can only be placed adjacent to a foundation.
[b]Windows[/b] – You can now craft a [b]Windowed Wall[/b]
[b]Torch[/b] – The torch functionality has now changed. When found, it will be permanently equipped and can be toggled with the torch key (default is [R]). Any torches that already exist in the game world will be destroyed, so you will have to find a new one for this to take effect. Please note that this will eventually be incorporated into a left hand item, so don’t worry die-hards - no floating torches here ;)
[b]Player Audio[/b] – A variety of new unique player character effects.
[b]Fish Trap[/b] – You can now craft a functioning [b]Fish Trap[/b]. At the moment it only catches fish, but we will expand on this in the future with crabs, crayfish, etc. What fish you catc

:: Beam Team

notes.title: LATEST UPDATE: 0.02
notes.notes:
Hi guys,

Version 0.02 is now live.
This week's update shouldn't require a restart, but if you notice any funny behavior please try starting a new game before posting a bug report.

[i][b]Please note that if you’re experiencing bugs such as stuck items on firepits, cooked cooked cooked items, etc, these bugs will persist until you start a new game as they have been saved in that state. [/b] [/i]


Stay Alive!
:: Beam Team
---


[h1][b]0.02 CHANGE LOG[/b][/h1]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[b]Key Bindings[/b] – Removed secondary key bindings which was interfering with AZERTY keyboard users.
[b]Menus[/b] – Fixed Audio Settings volume not applying when changed in-game.
[b]Menus[/b] – Fixed Mouse Sensitivity settings not applying when changed in-game.
[b]Menus[/b] – Fixed Input Menu’s scroll window position. 
[b]Inventory[/b] – Adjusted force when dropping items.
[b]Intro[/b] – Disabled dropping functionality for tutorial items to avoid confusion.
[b]Crafting[/b] – Fixed a bug where splitting an object with the dragging mechanic could stall the crafting system.
[b]Crafting[/b] – Fixed the possibility of saving mid-craft/build and reloading with the ghost item stuck on-screen. 
[b]Cooking[/b] – Fixed cookable item’s display name “Cooking” status spamming on every reload. Note: any previously saved cookables will still display as “Cooked Cooked Cooked", etc.
[b]Divers Slate[/b] - Fixed the Divers Slate holding position.
[b]Coconuts[/b] – Adjusted the coconut spawn amount.
[b]Coconuts[/b] – Coconuts viewing distance increased.
[b]Coconuts[/b] – Fixed a bug where you couldn't crack a coconut on another island.
[b]Fire Spit[/b] – Fixed a bug where if your inventory was full when picking something off the spit and then you made room and tried again, the item would not remove from the spit.
[b]Bed[/b] – Is now a normal craftable item. You can now drag it around into your home.
[b]Raft Motor[/b] – Fixed raft motor rotating further down with each reload.
[b]Raft Motor[/b] – Fixed various bugs with durability and speed.
[b]Raft Motor[/b] – Now has a fuel gauge.
[b]Airtank[/b] – Fixed infinite Airtank.
[b]Various[/b] – Fixed various item display names (goggles, flippers, martini, etc).
[b]Various[/b] – Fixed flying with dragging objects.
[b]Shadows[/b]– Fixed all construction objects that weren't displaying shadows.
[b]Harvestable Plants[/b] – Adjusted regrowth time.
[b]Bucket[/b] – Adjusted tipping angle, cooking time and fixed various cooking bugs.
[b]Lantern[/b] – Fixed a lighting bug with the lantern’s LOD and lighting masks.
[b]Watch[/b] – Minor rendering optimization and moved closer for easier reading.
[b]Land Sharks and Land Whales[/b] – Fixed.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Adjusted spawn amount.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Improved AI. Different shark species will flee from more dominant species. More aggressive in general.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Improved AI. Adjusted curiosity; Sharks tracking velocity increased. More aggressive stalking behavior.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Improved AI. Species are now more dependent on height, i.e: Great Whites will lurk below, Tiger sharks will roam on the surface.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Fixed a large bug with the sharks biomes.
[b]Sharks[/b] – More intense and aggressive attacking player animations,.
[b]Crabs[/b] – Adjusted the crab population amount. 
[b]Crabs[/b] – Adjusted crab calories vs. coconut calories.
[b]Crabs[/b] – Adjusted cooking time. 
[b]Fish[/b] – Fixed incorrect starting biomes. Fish species should now be correct for the current biome.
[b]Fish[/b] – Improvements and fixed a large bug with the fish system’s bounds checking.
[b]Audio[/b] – Higher bitrate rain sound.
[b]Audio[/b] – Adjusted Paddle sound.
[b]Audio[/b] – New drowning sound clip.
[b]Loot[/b] – Fixed duplicate loot items.
[b]Shipwrecks[/b] – Boat of doom no longer spawns on the shore.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[b]Menus[/b] – You can now choose to display temperature in Celsius or Fahrenheit.
[b]Temperature System[/b] – Stranded Deep now has a completely new temperature system running in the background. It’s based off real world values for the Pacific region. It takes the time, day, month, year and humidity into account when calculating the current temperature and apparent temperature (how hot it feels). The ocean temperature falls off with depth based on real-world values that have been scaled to the game world.  This system is still fairly fresh and will be incorporated more fully with your statistics in a future update (taking into account your exertion, whether you’re in shade, wet, etc).
[b]Inventory[/b] – The inventory now displays the property of the first item in a slots stack, i.e: health, durability, servings, etc. (Please note there’s a lot of different attributes for items so it’s possible some might not prioritize the right attribute).
[b]Turtle[/b] – New creature! 
[b]Sting Ray[/b] – New creature! 
[b]Blacktip Reef Shark[/b] – New creature!
[b]Lion Fish[/b] – New creature! 
[b]Fish[/b] – New creature! Clown Trigger Fish.
[b]Shipwrecks[/b] – New shipwrecks! Plane and ship bow.
[b]Door[/b] – New buildable item! You can now construct a door for your home, similar to a wall.
[b]Cloth[/b] – New item! You can now find cloth. This item is very much a placeholder and will be generally improved and integrated into more crafting combinations in the future.
[b]Crude Bandage[/b] – New item! You can now craft a [b]Crude Bandage[/b].


[i][b]Please note that if you're playing a saved game from a previous version, you will need to explore different biomes to find the new creatures, ie: previously saved islands will not have stingrays, turtles, etc but newly generated islands will.[/b][/i]

Hi guys,

Version 0.02 is now live.
This week's update shouldn't require a restart, but if you notice any funny behavior please try starting a new game before posting a bug report.

[i][b]Please note that if you’re experiencing bugs such as stuck items on firepits, cooked cooked cooked items, etc, these bugs will persist until you start a new game as they have been saved in that state. [/b] [/i]


Stay Alive!
:: Beam Team
---


[h1][b]0.02 CHANGE LOG[/b][/h1]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[b]Key Bindings[/b] – Removed secondary key bindings which was interfering with AZERTY keyboard users.
[b]Menus[/b] – Fixed Audio Settings volume not applying when changed in-game.
[b]Menus[/b] – Fixed Mouse Sensitivity settings not applying when changed in-game.
[b]Menus[/b] – Fixed Input Menu’s scroll window position. 
[b]Inventory[/b] – Adjusted force when dropping items.
[b]Intro[/b] – Disabled dropping functionality for tutorial items to avoid confusion.
[b]Crafting[/b] – Fixed a bug where splitting an object with the dragging mechanic could stall the crafting system.
[b]Crafting[/b] – Fixed the possibility of saving mid-craft/build and reloading with the ghost item stuck on-screen. 
[b]Cooking[/b] – Fixed cookable item’s display name “Cooking” status spamming on every reload. Note: any previously saved cookables will still display as “Cooked Cooked Cooked", etc.
[b]Divers Slate[/b] - Fixed the Divers Slate holding position.
[b]Coconuts[/b] – Adjusted the coconut spawn amount.
[b]Coconuts[/b] – Coconuts viewing distance increased.
[b]Coconuts[/b] – Fixed a bug where you couldn't crack a coconut on another island.
[b]Fire Spit[/b] – Fixed a bug where if your inventory was full when picking something off the spit and then you made room and tried again, the item would not remove from the spit.
[b]Bed[/b] – Is now a normal craftable item. You can now drag it around into your home.
[b]Raft Motor[/b] – Fixed raft motor rotating further down with each reload.
[b]Raft Motor[/b] – Fixed various bugs with durability and speed.
[b]Raft Motor[/b] – Now has a fuel gauge.
[b]Airtank[/b] – Fixed infinite Airtank.
[b]Various[/b] – Fixed various item display names (goggles, flippers, martini, etc).
[b]Various[/b] – Fixed flying with dragging objects.
[b]Shadows[/b]– Fixed all construction objects that weren't displaying shadows.
[b]Harvestable Plants[/b] – Adjusted regrowth time.
[b]Bucket[/b] – Adjusted tipping angle, cooking time and fixed various cooking bugs.
[b]Lantern[/b] – Fixed a lighting bug with the lantern’s LOD and lighting masks.
[b]Watch[/b] – Minor rendering optimization and moved closer for easier reading.
[b]Land Sharks and Land Whales[/b] – Fixed.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Adjusted spawn amount.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Improved AI. Different shark species will flee from more dominant species. More aggressive in general.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Improved AI. Adjusted curiosity; Sharks tracking velocity increased. More aggressive stalking behavior.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Improved AI. Species are now more dependent on height, i.e: Great Whites will lurk below, Tiger sharks will roam on the surface.
[b]Sharks[/b] – Fixed a large bug with the sharks biomes.
[b]Sharks[/b] – More intense and aggressive attacking player animations,.
[b]Crabs[/b] – Adjusted the crab population amount. 
[b]Crabs[/b] – Adjusted crab calories vs. coconut calories.
[b]Crabs[/b] – Adjusted cooking time. 
[b]Fish[/b] – Fixed incorrect starting biomes. Fish species should now be correct for the current biome.
[b]Fish[/b] – Improvements and fixed a large bug with the fish system’s bounds checking.
[b]Audio[/b] – Higher bitrate rain sound.
[b]Audio[/b] – Adjusted Paddle sound.
[b]Audio[/b] – New drowning sound clip.
[b]Loot[/b] – Fixed duplicate loot items.
[b]Shipwrecks[/b] – Boat of doom no longer spawns on the shore.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[b]Menus[/b] – You can now choose to display temperature in Celsius or Fahrenheit.
[b]Temperature System[/b] – Stranded Deep now has a completely new temperature system running in the background. It’s based off real world values for the Pacific region. It takes the time, day, month, year and humidity into account when calculating the current temperature and apparent temperature (how hot it feels). The ocean temperature falls off with depth based on real-world values that have been scaled to the game world.  This system is still fairly fresh and will be incorporated more fully with your statistics in a future update (taking into account your exertion, whether you’re in shade, wet, etc).
[b]Inventory[/b] – The inventory now displays the property of the first item in a slots stack, i.e: health, durability, servings, etc. (Please note there’s a lot of different attributes for items so it’s possible some might not prioritize the right attribute).
[b]Turtle[/b] – New creature! 
[b]Sting Ray[/b] – New creature! 
[b]Blacktip Reef Shark[/b] – New creature!
[b]Lion Fish[/b] – New creature! 
[b]Fish[/b] – New creature! Clown Trigger Fish.
[b]Shipwrecks[/b] – New shipwrecks! Plane and ship bow.
[b]Door[/b] – New buildable item! You can now construct a door for your home, similar to a wall.
[b]Cloth[/b] – New item! You can now find cloth. This item is very much a placeholder and will be generally improved and integrated into more crafting combinations in the future.
[b]Crude Bandage[/b] – New item! You can now craft a [b]Crude Bandage[/b].


[i][b]Please note that if you're playing a saved game from a previous version, you will need to explore different biomes to find the new creatures, ie: previously saved islands will not have stingrays, turtles, etc but newly generated islands will.[/b][/i]

notes.title: LATEST UPDATE: 0.01 HOTFIX
notes.notes:
Hi guys,

Hotfix 1 for version 0.01 (0.01.H1) is now live.
[i][b]Please note that you will need to start a new game as previous save files will not load correctly![/b][/i]

Stay Alive!
:: Beam Team
---


[h1][b]0.01.H1 CHANGE LOG[/b][/h1]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[b]Rafts[/b] - Fixed the “Bermuda Triangle” bug. Rafts no longer disappear when travelling.
[b]Rafts[/b] - Improved raft functionality with collisions and ladders.
[b]Player[/b] - Fixed a bug where the player would be reloaded inside the terrain, shipwrecks, etc.
[b]Player[/b] - Adjusted swimming speed.
[b]Intro[/b] - Fixed “Bouncing Betty” bug, see: http://steamcommunity.com/app/313120/discussions/1/613948093882138495/
[b]Cooking[/b] - Fixed campfires where multiple cookable items would interfere with each other’s cooking times.
[b]Menus[/b] - Fixed mouse sensitivity not applying.
[b]Menus[/b] - Added key binding functionality (Controllers are not officially supported, but it is possible).
[b]Menus[/b] - Added in-game options functionality.
[b]Saving/Terrain[/b] - Fixed a large bug; An edge case where if loading a saved game, and then resaving, previously saved biomes were being overwritten.
[b]Terrain[/b] - Adjusted rock and stick spawning quantity.
[b]Saving[/b] - Fixed a bug where stabbed items on the end of a Spear weren't being saved.
[b]Saving[/b] - Fixed item display names not saving.
[b]Sharks[/b] - Fixed disappearing great white sharks when killed.
[b]Sharks[/b] - Shouldn’t appear on land anymore..
[b]Sharks[/b] - Fixed shark meat not attaching to a Fire Spit.
[b]Sharks[/b] - Spear now damages sharks.
[b]Sharks[/b] - Various AI changes to increase the difficulty (a little).
[b]Marlin[/b] - Fixed disappearing Marlins when killed.
[b]Sleeping[/b] - Changed sleeping times. You can now sleep anytime from 6:00 pm to 6:00 am. The day count also increments properly now.
[b]Flare Gun[/b] - Fixed using spam.
[b]Harvesting Yuccas and Potatoes[/b] - Fixed incorrect scale of regrowing plants.
[b]Drinkable Coconut[/b] - Fixed using animations and audio with various tools.
[b]DeadEx Box[/b] - Can now be picked up.
[b]Container and Doors[/b] - Fixed audio spam when entering loaded biomes.
[b]Container and Doors[/b] - Fixed a large bug with loot spawning positions.
[b]Various[/b] - Fixed various missing interactive object tags, descriptions, etc.
[b]Various[/b] - Fixed the “Banana” yellow arm bug when looking at the watch and another lightsource was around.
[b]Various[/b] - Fixed a hovering bug with one of the glass shaders.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[b]Whales[/b] - New creature!
[b]Divers Slate[/b] - New Easter Egg!
[b]Boat Motor[/b] - Is now craftable and functional. Have fun with this one! ;)
